rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Table Setup 2.1 Number of Players 2.2 Game Mode 2.3 Game Speed 3 Gameplay 4 End of the Round and End of the Game Overview In 99 (addition card game) , counting is at stake as players play cards to the point total which always starts at 0. By playing cards in a strategic manner, players try to keep their lives without exceeding the number 99. When a player plays a card that goes over 99, they lose a life and the round is over. If a player loses all the lives, they are eliminated from the game. The player(s) with the most lives in the end win(s). Table Setup Number of Players This game can be played with 2-12 players in Board Game Arena. Various suggestions on optimal player count are as follows: Gaming Company Optimal Player Count Bicycle Cards 3-4 Board Game Arena 4 Board Game Geek 4-5 Game Mode This game can be played in two modes: Normal Mode : The ELO ranking will be calculated depending on the player count and game results. Training Mode : The game is simply played without taking the ELO ranking into account. Game Speed This game can be played in two systems, each with various speeds: Real-time : Slow / Normal / Fast Turn-based : Normal / Fast Gameplay At the start of the game, each player receives 3 lives and 3 random cards that form their hand. Meanwhile, the point total is set at 0 and the first player will be established. Gameplay occurs in rounds, starting with the first player. On their turn, the active player plays a card from their hand and alters the point total based on the card played: Card Type Played Effect on Point Total 2 3 5 6 7 8 Add face value A Add 1 or 11 J Q Add 10 4 Reverse the direction of play (No effect to point total - Add 0) 9 No effect (Add 0) 10 Subtract 10 K Set the point total at 99 After a card is played towards the point total, the active player draws a new card to add to their hand. The next player in clockwise order must play a card that does not put the total over 99 and draw a new one afterwards. End of the Round and End of the Game The round ends when a player busts and loses a life for failing to play a card that keeps the total within 99. After which, players receive a new hand of 3 cards for the next round. The point total sets back to 0 and the next round begins with the player who busted in the last round. Depending on the quick mode, the game could end in two ways: Quick Mode Disabled : When a player loses all the lives, that player is eliminated and the game continues. The last player with lives remaining wins. Quick Mode Enabled : When a player loses all the lives, that player is eliminated and the game ends. The player(s) with the most lives remaining win(s).

community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] A card addition game, play one card from your hand of three and try not to go over 99.  Some have special powers.  It would be relatively quick with 3p in real life. – Decision space is nearly always uninteresting, I felt like there was only 1 in 10 decisions that actually mattered

[Rating: 1/10] That was pretty awful. There isn't any room for mindgames in this, just stock up special cards that can save you from the 99. So in a weird way it reminds me of eurogames, just being efficient. But the thrill of traditional card games is skipped over, because there's no grand reveal or climax.

[Rating: 2/10] Could be a more interesting game if the preference order of cards wasn't so static: K > { 4, 9 } > 10 > A > 2 > 3 > 5 > 6 > 7 > 8 > { J, Q }

[Rating: 3/10] I played with kids who needed practice with addition, starting with the basic game (see Pagat.com)  and omitting any penalty of drinking alcohol, obviously. It was fine for that purpose.  We introduced special card powers one at a time. The kids liked it, but the game is an insubstantial luck-fest.

[Rating: 3/10] A card game where players try to be the last person standing. Players play a card, announce current sum, and draw a card. Cards may have powers, set the current sum to 99, reverse player order, etc. If the current sum is ever over 99, that player loses a life (starts with 3) and a new game wins. Once all but 1 player lose their lives, that player wins.

[Rating: 3/10] Pass, but could be bribed/coerced to play at 4 or 5 players. I rate this a bold 0 at 2 or 3 players.

[Rating: 4/10] Pointless exercise of counting from 0 to 99. Adding your own rules after each round is the only twist here.
